children: Bitcoin could remain stuck below $60,000 as long as fears around the durability of the AI trade persist and drag down U.S. stocks, Thahbib Rahman at Block Scholes says in a note. "Bitcoin's 90-day correlation to the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq-100 has rebuilt since reaching a year-to-date low in September." Bitcoin's current correlation is 53% to the S&P 500 and 54% to the Nasdaq-100, up from 37% and 36%, respectively, at the end of October and the highest since April, he says. Institutional demand has meanwhile weakened, with bitcoin exchange-traded funds seeing $4.94 billion of outflows so far in November, he says. Bitcoin falls 2.1% to $58,610, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
